summary: MAERI (Georgia Tech, ASPLOS 2018) builds a DNN accelerator from tiny configurable switches instead of a fixed PE array. A distribution tree multicasts operands to a row of multiplier switches; an augmented reduction tree sums their products. Because both networks are reconfigurable, multipliers can be grouped into 'virtual neurons' of any size, keeping utilisation high across irregular layer shapes.

p: Multiplier switches (MSs) sit in a 1D row and can either multiply or forward partial sums. A virtual neuron (VN) is a contiguous group of MSs that computes one output; its size follows the tile of the filter, so a 3×3×C filter and a fully connected row can both map without padding to a fixed array size.

A prefetch buffer feeds the distribution tree and stores partial sums when a filter is too large for one VN (folding): the partial sum is sent back through a forwarding MS and reduced with later results.

The distribution network is a bufferless binary tree that can unicast, multicast or broadcast in one traversal. The reduction network is a tree of adder switches with extra horizontal links between neighbouring nodes that have different parents; those links let several VNs reduce simultaneously without blocking each other. Each adder switch can add two or three inputs, or add one and forward another.
A tensor compute array whose dataflow is set by reconfigurable on-chip networks — closer to a flexible tensor datapath than to a general CGRA.

figures.title: MAERI datapath
figures.caption: Top: distribution tree from the prefetch buffer. Middle: 16 multiplier switches grouped into virtual neurons of sizes 5, 3, 6 and 2. Bottom: augmented reduction tree — dashed amber links are the augmented connections between neighbours with different parents.

caveats: Research architecture focused on configurable dataflow mappings; sizes are design parameters rather than a fixed chip.
